title: ⚠️ Threat notice Cisco NX-OS Nexus 3000 and 9000 Switches
description: Cisco NX-OS Software for Nexus 3000 and 9000 Series Switches contains a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-76471) in the NX-API feature. This flaw allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges or cause a denial of service by sending crafted HTTP requests. The NX-API feature is disabled by default on Nexus switches but enabled by default on UCS 6300 Series Fabric Interconnects through the UCS Manager XML API, which requires low-privileged user credentials. Cisco has released software updates to address this vulnerability, and no workarounds are available. Cisco also provides a temporary Live Protect shield mitigation. There are additional related vulnerabilities affecting Nexus switches disclosed in separate advisories. No public exploitation is known at this time.

aiSummary: CVE-2026-76471 is a critical remote code execution vulnerability in the NX-API feature of Cisco NX-OS Software running on Nexus 3000 and 9000 Series Switches and UCS 6300 Series Fabric Interconnects. The vulnerability arises from insufficient input validation of data sent to the NX-API, enabling an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges or cause process crashes leading to denial of service. Exploitation requires the NX-API feature to be enabled on Nexus switches, which is disabled by default, or valid low-privileged credentials on UCS 6300 devices. Cisco has released fixed software versions and a temporary Live Protect shield to mitigate the risk until updates can be applied. No workarounds exist. Cisco confirms no public exploitation or announcements of active attacks. Additional related critical vulnerabilities in NX-OS were disclosed concurrently in separate advisories.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on affected devices or cause denial of service through process crashes and device reloads. This can lead to full compromise of the network device and disruption of network operations. On UCS 6300 Series Fabric Interconnects, exploitation requires valid low-privileged user credentials, reducing the impact rating to high rather than critical. No public exploitation is currently known.
